title: Resulting part
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to [0.0, 0.0, -90.0] degrees and a translation vector of [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. On the first face, draw the first loop consisting of six lines: start from (0.0, 0.0) to (0.75, 0.0), then from (0.75, 0.0) to (0.75, 0.0443), next from (0.75, 0.0443) to (0.5312, 0.0443), followed by (0.5312, 0.0443) to (0.2198, 0.0443), then from (0.2198, 0.0443) to (0.0, 0.0443), and finally from (0.0, 0.0443) back to (0.0, 0.0). Apply a scaling factor of 0.75 to the entire two-dimensional sketch. Rotate the scaled sketch using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, -90.0] degrees and translate it using the vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Extrude the two-dimensional sketch 0.0448 units in the direction opposite to the normal to create a new solid body. The dimensions of the resulting part are 0.7499999812762963 units in length, 0.04426729161585327 units in width, and 0.04480540452418878 units in height.

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
sketch = sketch.rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), -90)

# Extrude the sketch
extrusion = sketch.extrude(0.0448)

# Final model

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · 1 sample
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0443, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0443, 0.0448) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0448) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
